draft.title: Why Britain colonised Australia
card: In the 1700s Britain sent many convicts to its American colonies. The American War of Independence ended this, as the colonies broke away from Britain.
British jails were crowded, so the government needed a new place to send convicts. Australia became that place.
Britain also wanted a base in the Pacific. A colony there could serve its ships and add to its power in the region.
The First Fleet carried convicts, marines and officials to Sydney Cove in 1788. This began the British colony of New South Wales.
draft.remember: Losing America left Britain with convicts and no place to send them, and a Pacific base was also wanted.

a.q: Which event made Britain look for a new place to send its convicts?
opts: The loss of its American colonies
The end of crowding in British jails
A rise in trade with the Pacific
The arrival of the First Fleet in 1788
a.why: Britain had sent convicts to America, and that stopped when the colonies broke away. The First Fleet is tempting, but it was the result of the search for a new place, not the cause.
a.clue: Where did Britain send convicts before Australia?

b.q: A student says, "Britain colonised Australia only to get rid of convicts." Which fact from the card shows this is incomplete?
opts: Britain also wanted a base for its ships in the Pacific
Britain had lost its colonies in America
The First Fleet reached Sydney Cove in 1788
British jails were crowded with convicts
b.why: A Pacific base was a second aim, so convicts were not the only reason. The other three facts are true, but they all relate to the convict problem or the date, so they do not add a second reason.
b.clue: Look for a reason that is not about convicts.

a.best: The loss of its American colonies

b.best: Britain also wanted a base for its ships in the Pacific
